capability_limits.detail: A `catchall` schema describes the extra keys an object may carry. The canonical record has no additional-properties slot, so it is recorded in `typescript_index` on the record; an object that is nothing but a `record` is modelled as a map.
A `brand` is a nominal tag that exists only in the type system. The branded schema is modelled with its constraints; the brand itself has no runtime or schema form.
`z.custom()` is a predicate over any value, with no structure to model. The declaration or member is left out of the model rather than widened to `any`.
A `z.function()` schema describes behaviour, not data. The declaration or member is left out of the model.
A `pipe` feeds one schema's output into another. The input schema is modelled; the schema it is piped into is not.
A `preprocess` step runs arbitrary code before parsing. The schema it feeds is modelled; what the step accepts and rewrites is not.
A `z.promise()` schema describes an asynchronous value, not a data shape. The declaration or member is left out of the model.
A `refine` / `superRefine` predicate is arbitrary code with no JSON Schema analogue. The schema it refines is modelled; the predicate itself is not, and this is where that is said.
A `transform` (and the `trim`, `toLowerCase` and `toUpperCase` string checks) changes the value after it is parsed. The *input* schema is modelled; the output shape the transform produces is not.

A tuple becomes a list whose items are the union of its element types, bounded by its length. Which type sits at which position is recorded in `typescript_tuple` — preserved and reportable, but not enforced by the canonical list.
